title: Prophecy
subtitle: Just a rumor, or a centuries-long scheme?

items.text: When black grass creeps, the children cry, a thousand fields where dead ones lie.
When thunder roars and dark clouds curl, the earth splits wide, the spirits swirl.
When the dragon glares, birds take flight. Yin twists with Yang, sun and moon unite.
UTTU Office
When Huanzhou falls, the immortal descends, granting longevity and the calamity's end.
Talk about inspiration! I'm using this as the introduction for my feature article. The mysterious vibe's gonna have them totally glued to the pages!
Got a whole lotta other stuff too. Gonna start as soon as I wrap up this fieldwork.
Trust me, Ms. Verity. This article's gonna be the star of UTTU's special issue on the East. I guarantee it!
As Reed provides her update, her voice shakes a delicate strand of spider silk before being carried off in the wind.
The two editors nod. One reaches out and gingerly touches the silk before them.

items.speaker: Verity
items.text: I think you really have something, Ms. Reed.

items.speaker: Verity
items.text: An elliptical rhyme concerning disasters and the secrets of longevity. It's no surprise that adventurers find it so intriguing.

items.speaker: Verity
items.text: But stories like this are not all that uncommon. I worry it won't have enough substance to carry our special issue.

items.speaker: Verity
items.text: What makes you so sure it's worth a field trip?

items.speaker: Reed
items.text: Ah, great question, ma'am. Well, I did some homework. It's not that much to go on, but if you'd just hear me out ...
The wind carries the sounds from the other side faithfully, even the soft noise of her turning pages.

items.speaker: Reed
items.text: There's been all kinds of mantic rhymes in China since, like, the dawn of recorded history, a lot of them obscure or ambiguous. Like, uh, here. There's this one about the Zhou dynasty: "He who sells bows and quivers shall bring the collapse of Zhou ..."

items.speaker: Reed
items.text: But really, it was the man's adopted daughter who married Emperor Yōu of Zhou and led to the empire's downfall, and she wasn't even the main cause! What I'm saying is, most of these mantic rhymes are laced with veiled analogies. Who knows what they could mean?

items.speaker: Reed
items.text: But this one's different—an exact event at an exact location. It's gonna be a breeze finding more details in the local annals. And my informant promised they'd give me more information when I get there.

items.speaker: Reed
items.text: So, yeah, this trip could be a bust, but I'll regret it for the rest of my life if I don't get to the bottom of it. So, here I am in Zhu County.

items.speaker: Reed
items.text: And guess what I found?
She pauses, savoring the suspense.

items.speaker: Reed
items.text: The wind really does slow around here! Only a little, but it for sure does!
The editors exchange surprised looks and lean in.

items.speaker: Barbara
items.text: Will you need any further assistance?

items.speaker: Reed
items.text: I'm all good for now. But I'll let you guys know.

items.speaker: Reed
items.text: First, I've gotta contact my informant and set up a meeting. Then, I'll interview some locals on the street.

items.speaker: Reed
items.text: Who knows? We could even find another shelter if things go well.
She's so eager to share her plans that she fails to notice her colleagues have fallen quiet.

items.speaker: Verity
items.text: She's always been a go-getter in every life.

items.speaker: Barbara
items.text: But I worry for her. You know how obsessed she is about longevity. These clues she found are unlikely to be a coincidence.

items.speaker: Verity
items.text: You needn't worry. Reed grew up there, originally. She won't have any trouble getting accustomed.

items.speaker: Verity
items.text: But let's keep an eye on her, just to be sure.
The woolly editor holds her worried expression. Verity returns it with a silent pleading glance, motioning toward the still-open silk.
Street, Zhu County

items.speaker: Barbara
items.text: Reed? Are you still there?

items.speaker: Barbara
items.text: We trust you've made a good decision with this article, but our network isn't stable right now. You'd better ...
The noise from the streets drowns out the rest of her words.

items.speaker: Reed
items.text: My bad. Didn't mean to block the way!

items.speaker: Reed
items.text: Cool, cool, gotta go! I'm racing against the clock here! Call you later.

items.speaker: Barbara
items.text: Watch out ... danger.

items.speaker: Reed
items.text: No worries. I'll be careful. Bye bye!
Reed ends the connection, adjusting her spiderweb brooch as she dodges through the crowds of people and passing bikes.
She looks around and spies her goal not far away.

items.speaker: Reed
items.text: Hate to hang up on you, Barbara, but I've got, like, no time to do this. Maybe I'll buy her some local delicacies to say sorry.

items.speaker: Reed
items.text: Place sure is lively, so many stores, oh my God, and the restaurants! Finally, no more driving to Chinatown to get a decent meal.

items.speaker: Reed
items.text: Alright, first things first. Gotta find an Internet cafe to contact the informant. Oh, better get a couple bottles of water too.
The grass-headed editor walks toward the sign across the street.
An electric fan oscillates back and forth, attempting in vain to blow away the heat rising from the road.
Reed rests on a bamboo chair, her hand finding the mouse in a familiar motion.
Endless Stream BBS
She processes the new information, immediately drawing up a mental map of her impending investigation.

items.speaker: Reed
items.text: Nice and clear. Let's go.
Reed takes a confident step forward.

items.speaker: Reed
items.text: Excuse me. Do you know the way to Jīn's Well? It's under a tree by the Paifang.

items.speaker: Middle-Aged Woman
items.text: What well? Never heard of it.

items.speaker: Middle-Aged Woman
items.text: If you're looking for scenic spots, go to the outskirts of town. There's a lot of beautiful sculptures and architecture out there.

items.speaker: Middle-Aged Woman
items.text: And the Mei trees in the central park are famous. But I don't know anything about a well.

items.speaker: Reed
items.text: Oh, thanks. I'll check them out later.
She waves goodbye to the fifteenth kind person she has questioned so far. The information she's been hoping for still fails to arrive.
Standing in the heart of Zhu County, she lets her eyes wander from the new unfinished buildings rising in the east over to the ancient horse-head walls in the west.

items.speaker: Reed
items.text: Jianshe Road ...
The street sign's metallic glare blinds her for a moment.

items.speaker: Reed
items.text: That's it. I've asked everyone on the street. No well, no stall, no Grandma Wáng.

items.speaker: Reed
items.text: There's no way I got the address wrong. Did my informant lie? Not likely. What good would that do them?

items.speaker: Reed
items.text: The northern custom house, the Great Buddha Temple, Jianshe Road, Renmin Road ...
The locations feel off to the young editor. Each one seems to have no connection to the others.

items.speaker: Reed
items.text: What if these are all old locations? Like, they're names of places from the past?

items.speaker: Elder
items.text: Hey, young comrade. What are you doing in the middle of the street?
A voice speaks, bringing a tide of relief that washes over her like soft rain.

items.speaker: Elder
items.text: You've been asking around for directions, haven't you? To the bus stop? Just follow me. I'm heading there right now.

items.speaker: Reed
items.text: No, no. I'm meeting someone by Jīn's Well. Do you know where that is?

items.speaker: Reed
items.text: Could be an old name, like, really, really old. So, if you know of anywhere even kinda similar, that'd be great. Anything will do.

items.speaker: Elder
items.text: Jīn's Well, Jīn's Well ... I've lived here almost 60 years and never heard of it.

items.speaker: Reed
items.text: Then, it might be more than 60 years old. Maybe a hundred or so?

items.speaker: Elder
items.text: 100 years old? You've got to be kidding. Things change so fast. The whole county looks completely different every few decades, let alone a century.

items.speaker: Elder
items.text: You're not trying to pull a fast one on me, are you? I thought you needed help.

items.speaker: Reed
items.text: No, sorry.
She considers each piece of information, trying to find a path through their mutual confusion.

items.speaker: Reed
items.text: Oh, wait, the rhyme! Have you ever heard of this rhyme?

items.speaker: Reed
items.text: It's about black grass, thunder, the earth opening up, and an immortal.

items.speaker: Elder
items.text: What? A rhyme?
The scorn in his voice is withering.
For a moment, the approaching deadline and her still blank pages seem like a freight train rushing toward her.

items.speaker: Elder
items.text: Aren't you a little too old to be searching for things from fairy tales?

items.speaker: Elder
items.text: But I have heard it before—an immortal that slept deep beneath Zhu County. In ancient times when the sky shattered and the earth broke apart, they emerged to save the town.

items.speaker: Elder
items.text: But the immortal disappeared right after, taking the Method of Longevity with them, and no one has ever figured out where they went.

items.speaker: Elder
items.text: Still, grave robbers turn up around here every year. Those troublemakers just won't give up.

items.speaker: Elder
items.text: You seem like a bright young lady. Surely you don't buy into this longevity nonsense, right?
